newsitem.title: ITALY: Armani embroiders lustre into wintry evenings.
newsitem.headline: Armani embroiders lustre into wintry evenings.

text.p: Top Italian designer Giorgio Armani unveiled a dazzling display of sequin-embroidered evening gowns as the closing flourish to Milan's autumn/winter 1997/98 fashion shows on Sunday.
Armani's top line ready-to-wear designs included dense jet beading, heavy encrusting of silver sequins, sparkling lace and crystal borders on lightweight chiffon and fluid black velvet.

"The silhouette, the style, the desire for refinement all become even more pronounced in the long evening dresses where embroidery and discreet transparencies represent the striking feature of the season," Armani said.
Sequinning was at times so closeknit it gave garments a liquid, metallic finish while some dark fabrics were worked with occasional pinprick sequins like stars on a matt background.
Evening dresses were long, including one designed with a jet beaded halterneck over a full-length velvet skirt. Calf or full length skirts were also worn over sheer, loose-cut leggings.
Colours were dark -- predominantly black -- and relieved by the sequins, but the final piece was a shimmering red full-length gown and light coat worn with a tiny jet cap and feathers.
Velvet played a key role, black horizontal panels alternating with black transparent panels for trousers, tops and dresses or left solid to play against crystal sequinning.

It also played a part for daywear, with gold flowering printed on the sleek finish for a jacket, velvet wraps with fine, floor length fringes, or narrow-ribbed black velvet with a blue sheen used for a long jacket.
Trouser suits were a stalwart of daytime designs, with jackets which followed the curve of the body closely to the hip or mid-thigh and straight, easy-fitting trousers to the ankle.
Some jackets buttoned at one side, often with concealed fastenings, while others were cut wide and kimono-like, with broad sleeves, coming in satiny emerald green or purple.
Armani's presentation, held as usual at his elegant palazzo in central Milan, marks the end of the eight days of shows.

Styles have varied but retail buyers say the broad trend is for a return to wider, padded shoulders from a recent narrow shouldered 1970s look, giving a hard edge of masculine tailoring which is offset by feminine touches like high stiletto heels.
Glamour is also back, with accessories like feather boas and fur trims to hems, cuffs and lapels on the increase.
Many major designers left their collections under wraps until the tail end of the week, drawing a mixture of show business celebrities such as American actress Andie MacDowell.

Designer Gianni Versace, who presented his line-up on Saturday, attracted famous names like British actor Hugh Grant and girlfriend Elizabeth Hurley, action movie star Jean-Claude Van Damme, singer Boy George as well as supermodels Naomi Campbell and Eva Herzigova, accompanied by husband Tico Torres.
Earlier in the week, American jazz artist Ray Charles performed at Salvatore Ferragamo's show.
